messages.subject: .cwa file not opening
parts:
Hi,
I just started using the package, with a .csv file in the data directory I get the following error:

Part 1
[1] "File name: 001.csv"
[1] "P1 file1"
[1] "---------------------------------------------"
[1] "investigate calibration of the sensors..."
Error in if (sf == 0) sf = 80 : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

With a binary .cwa file in the folder
_____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
Part 1
[1] "Error: File path not clearly identified. Check path name"
[1] "no files to analyse"
[1] "File name: NA"
Error in `[<-`(`*tmp*`, j, 1, value = NA_character_) : 
  subscript out of bounds

Any clue on what I am doing wrong? Any suggestions would be greatly appreciated.

Added the section the script

library(GGIR)
# INPUT NEEDED from user
f0=1
f1=2
mode=c(1)
datadir="C:/Batch_schizophrenia/Data"
outputdir="C:/Batch_schizophrenia/Results"
studyname="Data"
g.shell.GGIR(#=======================================
             #General parameter
             mode=mode,
             datadir = datadir,
             outputdir=outputdir,
             studyname=studyname,
             f0=f0,
             f1=f1,
             overwrite = TRUE,
             do.imp=TRUE,
             idloc=TRUE,
             print.filename=TRUE,
             storefolderstructure=FALSE,
             
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 1:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: reading file, auto-calibration, and extracting features
             windowsizes=c(5,900,3600),
             do.cal=TRUE,
             do.enmo = TRUE,             
             do.anglez=TRUE,
             chunksize=1,
             printsummary=TRUE)

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] .cwa file not opening
parts: The error message you get should be a hint:
[1] "Error: File path not clearly identified. Check path name"

In addition, the fact that GGIR did not manage to retrieve the filename as indicated by:
[1] "File name: NA"
hints at the file directory not being correctly specified, there is no file in the directory, or there is a problem with access permissions.

Vincent
